hero.body:
Vero Beach High School has scheduled a football matchup against Atlantic High School for August 28, 2026, according to Sports Illustrated. The game will be hosted by Vero Beach as the school builds out its fall season schedule. This contest falls in the opening weeks of the 2026 football season, giving both teams an early-season opportunity to compete against area opponents.

The Atlantic at Vero Beach game is part of a broader schedule that Vero Beach has confirmed for the upcoming fall. The school previously announced a match against Jensen Beach on August 21, 2026, which comes one week before the Atlantic matchup. These early-season games position Vero Beach to test itself against local competition as teams prepare for the remainder of their schedules.

Beyond the Atlantic game, Vero Beach has additional contests lined up for the season. The Indian River County school will host Central High School on September 25, 2026, continuing its schedule of area matchups. These games represent a mix of opponents from the region as Vero Beach works to create a competitive slate for fall competition.

The August 28 game between Atlantic and Vero Beach provides both programs with an opportunity to begin their 2026 seasons on the field. With multiple games confirmed through late September, Vero Beach appears focused on establishing a schedule anchored by regional opponents. Atlantic's trip to Vero Beach marks one of several contests that will define the early portion of the fall football season in Indian River County.

cards.headline: Marcus & Millichap brokers $5.3 million sale of Vero Beach apartment property
cards.teaser: A multifamily property in Vero Beach sold for $5.3 million in a transaction brokered by Marcus & Millichap.
cards.body:
Marcus & Millichap announced the sale of a multifamily property in Vero Beach for $5.3 million. The transaction was completed on Wednesday, July 1, 2026.

The real estate investment brokerage firm handled the sale of the apartment complex in the Indian River County city.

The sale represents continued investment activity in Vero Beach's residential real estate market. Marcus & Millichap specializes in commercial real estate sales and financing.

cards.headline: Florida school grades released with Indian River County scoring high marks
cards.teaser: Indian River County schools received high scores in the state's annual school grade release, along with St. Lucie and Martin counties.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Education released school grades on Wednesday, with Indian River County schools scoring high marks. St. Lucie and Martin counties also performed well in the annual assessment.

The grades measure school performance based on student achievement and learning gains. Indian River County joined its neighboring Treasure Coast counties in earning strong results for the school year.

The release came on July 1, 2026, providing parents and educators with performance data for the previous academic year. Specific grade breakdowns by individual schools were included in the state's report.

cards.headline: Vero Beach to host Central High School in football game September 25
cards.teaser: Vero Beach High School will face Central High School in a football matchup scheduled for September 25, 2026.
cards.body:
Vero Beach High School has scheduled a football game against Central High School for September 25, 2026. The matchup was announced Wednesday as part of the upcoming football season schedule.

The game will be played at Vero Beach as teams prepare for the fall 2026 season. Vero Beach has also scheduled games against Jensen Beach on August 21 and Atlantic High School on August 28.

The football schedule reflects Vero Beach's slate of opponents for the 2026 season. Additional details about game times and ticket information will be released as the season approaches.

cards.headline: Jensen Beach to play at Vero Beach in August 21 football game
cards.teaser: Jensen Beach High School will travel to Vero Beach for a football game on August 21, 2026.
cards.body:
Jensen Beach High School is scheduled to play at Vero Beach High School on August 21, 2026, in a football matchup announced Wednesday. The game is part of the early season schedule for both teams.

The contest will mark one of the opening games for both schools as they begin the 2026 football season. Jensen Beach, located in Martin County, will face the Indian River County squad in late August.

Vero Beach High School has lined up multiple opponents for the upcoming season. The school's football program continues to draw competition from across the Treasure Coast region.

cards.headline: Man arrested after driving truck into Indian River County convenience store
cards.teaser: A man was arrested Wednesday after driving a truck into a convenience store in Indian River County.
cards.body:
A man was arrested Wednesday after driving a truck into a convenience store in Indian River County. The incident occurred on July 1, 2026, and resulted in an arrest.

Indian River County deputies responded to the scene after the vehicle crashed into the building. The driver was taken into custody following the crash.

Authorities have not released the name of the suspect or the specific location of the convenience store. The circumstances that led to the vehicle entering the building remain under investigation.

No information has been provided about injuries or the extent of damage to the store. The case remains active as deputies continue their investigation into the incident.

cards.headline: New Florida law opens affordable housing funding to manufactured home repairs
cards.teaser: A new state law that took effect Wednesday expands affordable housing funds to help mobile and manufactured home owners pay for emergency repairs and storm hardening.
cards.body:
Senate Bill 594 took effect July 1st, opening $167 million in state affordable housing funding to mobile and manufactured home owners for emergency repairs and storm-hardening retrofits. The law follows an investigation that found nearly 700,000 manufactured homes in Florida, about two-thirds of the state's more than 1 million mobile and manufactured homes, were built before current federal safety standards and cannot withstand modern storms.

The legislation was prompted by an EF-3 tornado that destroyed 138 homes at Spanish Lakes Country Club Community in Fort Pierce, killing six residents. Many seniors living in older manufactured homes cannot afford repairs that cost $10,000 to $15,000. Under the new law, about 75 percent of counties' annual SHIP funding could help eligible mobile and manufactured homeowners. Indian River County officials said staff will take an item regarding the legislative change to the Board on August 18, with a September 30 deadline to submit its plan to the state. Martin County's online application portal opens in August, with eligible homeowners able to apply online or by mail.
